Reviewer_Notes: All three versions preserve the main facts, names, locations and the eight-warrant detail. English sentences are understandable. Some transitions between Hindi and English are abrupt, and 'externed from the district' is formal. Sentence-level mixing does not create natural within-sentence Hinglish.

Translated sentences preserve the main meaning, names and numerical details. However, Hindi fragments such as 'मौत' and 'समाप्त' remain in the mixed text and interrupt readability. The 30% and 50% versions are nearly identical, so their actual mixing levels should be checked.
Main facts, names and October dates are preserved across all versions. English sentences are understandable, although Hindi-English transitions are sometimes abrupt.

Main election results, candidate names and vote margins in translated sentences are preserved. Several paragraphs remain in Hindi, including in the 50% version. Mixing coverage and transitions are uneven.
Translated sentences preserve the main details, names, dates, locations and diplomatic issues. English is understandable, though some transitions are abrupt.

Translated sentences preserve the main reported statements and political details. Much of the article remains in Hindi, and transitions are uneven. The article reports a denial of the newspaper's claim, not confirmation of Al-Sisi's candidacy.

Main political details and names are mostly preserved in translated sentences. Several paragraphs remain in Hindi. The source opening itself is confusing about Jaswant Singh, and the mixed versions retain this ambiguity.
Names, five suspects and the December 27 date are preserved. The 10% version contains no English replacement. Higher-level versions have understandable English, although some sentences are long.

The main announcement, 16 countries, estimate of more than 25 million overseas Indians and conference details are preserved. The 10% version contains no English replacement. Higher-level versions are understandable.

Translated passages preserve the voter estimate, 645 contested seats, 324-seat majority, party seat counts and historical turnout figures. English is readable and the main numerical details are consistent with the source.
The February 1, 2006 start date, December 2004 restoration decision and historical details are preserved in translated passages. English is readable, with some sentence-level language switching.
Translated passages preserve match history, scores, player names, retirement details and World Cup statistics. English is understandable, although language switching remains sentence-level.
The 45-member NSG, trust vote and 14 of 22 nuclear facilities are preserved. The final English sentence about civilian use is awkwardly phrased. The 10% version has limited English coverage.
Translated passages preserve the reported deaths, 230,000 security personnel, candidate names, polling estimates and election issues. The 10% version contains no English replacement.
The Rs 10,000 cash withdrawal and Rs 10 tax calculation are preserved. The income-tax thresholds remain in Hindi in all versions, so English coverage is incomplete.
The translated passages preserve the names, location of arrest and reported events. The 10% version contains no English replacement. The higher-level versions are understandable.

The 550 km distance, 70 km per hour wind speed and 75,000 evacuees are preserved. The source repeats the evacuation figure, and the mixed versions retain this repetition. The 10% version contains no English replacement.

Main events, names and allegations are preserved in the translated passages. Details about police action, injuries to students, the government's position and possible Maoist involvement remain partly or entirely in Hindi.
